sections.h2: Where is DeWitt, and what kind of town is it?
sections.html:
DeWitt sits in Onondaga County along Syracuse's eastern side and has 33.7 square miles of land. The town was carved out of Manlius in 1835 and named for Major Moses DeWitt, a judge and soldier, according to the town's own history page.

The Erie Canal opened through the area in 1825, and a railroad reached East Syracuse in 1839. The New York Central bought land in 1872 for the rail yards that grew into the village of East Syracuse, which sits inside the town. DeWitt's population peaked near 29,000 in 1970, and the town now describes about 25,000 residents plus roughly 43,000 people who work there each day.

The named hamlets are DeWitt, Collamer, Franklin Park, Jamesville, Lyndon Corners and Oot Park. For a buyer, the hamlet name matters less than the school district and the tax bills attached to a parcel, so lead with those in an ad.

sections.h2: How large is DeWitt, and what do its homes sell for?
sections.html:
QuickFacts, the Census Bureau's profile of the town, gives 25,487 residents for mid-2025, down 2.3 percent from its 2020 base. Every number in the list is drawn from town profile.

  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 73.6 percent
  • Typical home value in the five-year survey ending 2024: $243,500
  • Typical household income: $92,218
  • Typical monthly rent: $1,042
  • Average trip to work: 17.6 minutes
  • Adults with a four-year degree: 49.0 percent

Because values vary by neighborhood and school district, price a DeWitt house against recent sales near it and not against a countywide figure.

sections.h2: Which roads and employers matter to a DeWitt sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 81 cuts through the center of DeWitt, crossing Interstate 690 on the east side and the Thruway (I-90) in the north. Route 5 and 92 run together across the east side, Route 173 crosses the south through Jamesville, and Route 298 and Route 290 cross the north and middle. Half of Syracuse Hancock International Airport lies inside the town's northwest corner.

The town's employer list includes the Carrier engineering and design center, the headquarters of Community Bank on Widewaters Parkway, the Jamesville quarry, and Le Moyne College, which holds most of its academic buildings in DeWitt. Aspen Dental was founded here too. A commute of 17.6 minutes on average suggests many residents work close to home, which is a fair point to make in a listing.

Parts of DeWitt belong to four public districts: Jamesville-DeWitt, East Syracuse-Minoa, Fayetteville-Manlius and North Syracuse. The town's tax office says three of them bill school taxes on DeWitt parcels, and its STAR comparison table lists Jamesville-DeWitt, East Syracuse-Minoa and Fayetteville-Manlius.

Private options in town include Bishop Grimes Junior/Senior High School, Christian Brothers Academy, Manlius Pebble Hill School and the Syracuse Hebrew Day School. Check the district on your tax bill before you write a listing, since a street can sit on a district line.

sections.h2: When are DeWitt property taxes due, and which dates matter to a seller?
sections.html:
School taxes are collected in September and town and county taxes in January, with no interest charged inside those windows. The Receiver of Taxes handles roughly 11,000 parcels, and the assessor's calendar runs on a separate track.

DeWitt assessment and tax calendar
WhenWhat happens
March 1Deadline to file every exemption application
May 1Tentative assessment roll filed
4th Tuesday of MayGrievance Day, with forms due at the office by 8:00 pm
July 1Final roll filed
Early SeptemberSchool tax bills mailed, payable that month
End of DecemberTown and county bills mailed, payable in January

Source: Town of DeWitt Assessor and Tax Department pages. The next town and county bills are mailed at the end of December, so a house closing in late 2026 or early 2027 will usually need a tax proration at the table.

sections.h2: What happens to exemptions and tax bills when a DeWitt house sells?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office administers STAR, senior, veterans, disability, clergy and agricultural exemptions, and any mailing address change goes through that office rather than the tax office.

The town's 2024 comparison puts the Enhanced STAR credit between $1,613 and $1,857 depending on the school district, and the Basic STAR credit between about $652 and $697. Ask the Assessor how a change of owner affects a STAR benefit.

  • Tax bills for escrowed loans go to the bank, so a seller should not expect a paper copy.
  • If a bill arrives after you sell, forward it to the new owner or return it to the tax office with a note.
  • Mail payments from inside a post office and ask for a hand cancellation, since meter stamps do not count as a postmark.
  • Printed bills and past receipts are available through the Onondaga County Real Property Tax Services site.

sections.h2: Does a DeWitt seller need permits, a certificate of occupancy or flood information?
sections.html:
Almost any improvement to real property except minor repairs needs a permit from Planning and Zoning. A complete application includes a survey (photos are not accepted), a signed estimate, two sets of plans, and proof of disability and workers' compensation coverage. Work over $20,000 must carry a licensed professional's stamp.

A certificate of occupancy applies to new construction, alterations and conversions where people will live, and a certificate of compliance applies to items like pools, fences, sheds, garages and fireplaces. Pull these records early. A deck or finished basement with no paperwork is a gap a buyer's attorney will find.

Flood maps matter too. FEMA's updated flood insurance rate maps for Onondaga County took effect on November 4, 2016, and some properties were placed in a high-risk zone for the first time. Paper copies are kept at the Planning and Zoning office at Town Hall.

sections.h2: Which state transfer rules apply to a DeWitt closing?
sections.html:
The state taxes a transfer at two dollars for each $500 of price. The TP-584 return and payment go to the county clerk by the 15th day after the deed changes hands. Buyers of homes priced at $1 million and up owe an added 1 percent, as the state's transfer tax page explains.

Ask the Onondaga County Clerk for current recording fees, and let your closing attorney confirm who pays what under the contract.

sections.h2: Which routes give DeWitt sellers the quickest exit?
sections.html:
Sellers can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take an offer from a buyer paying cash. The cash route tends to close fastest because there is no mortgage underwriting, though the offer will reflect the speed and any repairs the buyer takes on.

Whatever you pick, collect the permit history, tax status, district name and flood zone details first. Those four items answer most early questions and keep a DeWitt closing moving.

faqs.q: What does a typical DeWitt home cost?
faqs.a: About $243,500, according to the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey data. Households there earn $92,218 in the middle of the range, and owners live in 73.6 percent of homes.

faqs.q: When do DeWitt school taxes come due?
faqs.a: They are payable during September, and bills go out in the first days of that month. The town and county levy follows in January, with bills mailed late in December to owners who do not escrow.
The town Assessor's office. It takes exemption applications, renewals and mailing address changes, and the filing cutoff for every exemption is March 1.

faqs.q: Does permit history affect a DeWitt sale?
faqs.a: It can. The town requires permits for most improvements and issues a certificate once the work passes its final inspection, so open permits or missing certificates can slow a closing. Ask Planning and Zoning what is on file for your address.

faqs.q: Where is a DeWitt deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Onondaga County Clerk's office. The state transfer tax return travels with the deed and is due there by the 15th day after delivery.
